outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Efficient Attention Mechanisms
outline.description: This chapter establishes the motivation for the research by defining the transformer architecture, identifying attention as the computational bottleneck in long-context scenarios, and reviewing the evolution of optimization strategies from standard implementations to FlashAttention.
subtopics: The role of Self-Attention in Transformers and its quadratic complexity problem
Implications for Long-Context Applications (documents, codebase, multimodal)
Review of existing solutions: Approximation methods vs. Software Optimization
Evolutionary History: Standard Attention -> FlashAttention -> FlashAttention-2
Identifying the Gap: Why FlashAttention-2 still underutilizes modern H100 hardware

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Hardware Architecture and Execution Models
outline.description: A deep dive into the specific GPU hardware capabilities required for FlashAttention-3, focusing on the NVIDIA Hopper architecture, memory hierarchies, asynchronous execution units, and low-precision arithmetic formats.
subtopics: GPU Memory Hierarchies: GMEM, L2 Cache, Shared Memory (SRAM), and Registers
Thread Hierarchy: Warps, Thread Blocks (CTA), and Warp Groups in Hopper
Asynchronous Units: The Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) and Async WGMMA instructions
Warp-Specialization Concepts: Producer-Consumer patterns for latency hiding
Low-Precision Formats: Understanding FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) vs. FP16/BF16
